## Purpose
`AgentCmd` (`agent/cli.rs`) and `CapabilityCmd` (`capability/cli.rs`) are two of the 19 `{Family}Cmd` enums that `RunCmd` flattens via `#[command(flatten)]` so every subcommand stays flat (`mustard-rt run <name>`, never `run <family> <name>`). Each family's `cli.rs` owns exactly one such enum plus its `dispatch()` function — this is the CLI-registration half of a subcommand family, distinct from the entry-point logic itself.

## Convention
Folder: apps/rt/src/commands/** · Extension: .rs · Files of this role in this subproject: 19
Both exemplars open with the identical boilerplate header explaining the "TWO registrations" rule (enum variant + dispatch arm) and the flat-naming contract. The enum derives `#[derive(Debug, Subcommand)]` with `#[allow(clippy::large_enum_variant)]` (documented as unavoidable — boxing breaks the clap derive). Every variant carries `#[command(display_order = N)]` pinning its historical slot in `run --help`, and a full doc comment on the variant describing its exact behavior/flags (this doc comment is what `--help` shows, so it is user-facing prose, not internal commentary). `dispatch()` is a flat `match cmd { ... }` delegating one line per variant into the family's real entry module.

## How to apply
A new family gets its own `cli.rs` with a `{Family}Cmd` enum (never reuse another family's enum) and a `dispatch()` matching every variant. A new subcommand within an existing family adds a variant with the next free `display_order` plus a `dispatch()` arm — both edits are mandatory (the CLAUDE.md guard: forgetting the arm compiles but the command vanishes). `RunCmd` in `commands/mod.rs` only flattens; it must never gain command logic of its own.
